title: Clinical characteristics, treatment patterns and survival of individuals with adenocarcinoma of the stomach (ICD-10 C16) or the gastro-oesophageal junction (ICD-10 C15.5) in Germany - a study based on cancer registry data (VONKO-022)
summary:
Stomach cancer is one of the most common and most dangerous types of cancer in the world. In 2022, around 4.9% of all new cancer diagnoses and 6.8% of all cancer deaths were due to stomach cancer. In Germany, only around 33-37% of those patients survive the first five years after diagnosis.

The junction between the oesophagus and stomach is known as the gastro-oesophageal junction. Cancer in this area is very similar to stomach cancer in the upper part of the stomach (cardia), as the two areas are close together. Like stomach cancer, oesophageal cancer has become increasingly common since the 1970s. It used to be difficult to diagnose oesophageal cancer as there were no standardized criteria for assessment. This probably led to misdiagnosis and underdiagnosis.

There are more and more new treatment options for stomach cancer and cancer at the junction of the stomach and the oesophagus. These include immunotherapies and targeted antibodies. These are currently being tested in trials and are already being used in some cases. In order to optimize the use of these therapiesoptimally, we need to better understand how the treatments work and what results they achieve in everyday life.

This study looks back at how stomach cancer and cancer at the junction of the stomach and the oesophagus are treated in Germany. Data stored in cancer registries will be used for this purpose. These are data from real-life care, not study data. The aim is to find out more about the patientsfor example, how old they are and gender they are. It is also about the treatments, possible side effects and complications as well as the survival.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm: Lower third of oesophagus

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of cancer registry data of cases of adenocarcinoma of the stomach or gastro-oesophageal junction from the diagnosis years 2014-2023 (observational study)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- ICD-10 C15.5 and ICD-10 C15.5
- Histological type adenocarcinoma: ICD-O-3 8140-8149, 8160-8162, 8190-8221, 8260-8337, 8350-8551, 8570-8576, 8940-8941
- Diagnosis years 2014-2023
- For diagnosis place of residence in the federal state of the requested registry ‘residence-related cases’)
Exclusion criteria:
- Patients diagnosed with any other primary malignancy (except non-melanoma skin cancer; ICD-10 code C44) within 5 years prior to gastric/GOJ AC. 
- Cancer cases known to the registry based exclusively on i) a post-mortem certificate (DCO case), ii) a pathology or progress report, iii) a report on the tumour conference, or iv) a combination of the aforementioned notification types
